name: THE BAKEHOUSE
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE OVEN
LOOK_AT: A brick oven, built big and lit early. Bread for a town of two thousand comes out of one door.
The bricks round the door are scorched black, and the bricks round that are scorched brown. It has been working for years.
A long wooden paddle hangs beside it, worn pale at the handle. That paddle has fed the whole town.
LISTEN_TO: Warm. Working. Something in this town is *working*.
The fire roaring low in the back of it, steady as a mill.
A loaf, somewhere inside, crackling as it cools. Good bread talks.

overrides.OPEN: Not with my hands, and not with my face. It's a professional oven.

subjects.name: THE FLOUR
LOOK_AT: Flour sacks stacked to the rafters, with the flour on everything else as well. Including, now, me.
The sacks are stamped from Sacramento. Flour travels better than men do, and arrives in a better mood.
There are small white footprints across the floor from the sacks to the table, all day's worth of them.
LISTEN_TO: A sack settling, very softly. Flour has a hush to it.
Nothing. A sack of flour is the most patient object in the world.
A sift of it falling from a shelf, like a little snow.

subjects.name: THE TABLE
LOOK_AT: A long table, floured and scraped, with the dough laid out in rows. The only rows in Consolation that come out even.
The wood's been scraped down so many times there's a dip in the middle. Bread made the dip.
Every loaf on it is the same size. Somebody weighs them. In this town that's practically a confession of honesty.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Dough rises without saying anything about it. I admire that.
Dough being slapped down at the far end, and folded, and slapped again.
Nothing for a moment, and then a knife through a crust.

overrides.PICK_UP: Not the bread. Not the dough. Not even the flour. I can tell from the boy's back.

subjects.name: THE BOY
LOOK_AT: A boy with flour to the elbows, carrying a tray twice his width and not dropping anything. He has not looked up once.
He works like a man paid by the loaf and proud of the rate.
Flour in his hair, flour in his eyebrows. In ten years he'll be gray, and nobody will notice the difference.
LISTEN_TO: He's humming, in time with the kneading. The tune is wrong. The time is perfect.
Still humming. The same wrong tune, kept beautifully.
His breath, steady, keeping time with the dough. He'd make a good metronome.

overrides.TALK_TO: He's counting under his breath. If I speak, he'll lose count, and then we'll both be lost.

subjects.name: THE BACK DOOR
LOOK_AT: The back door, propped open with a brick to let the heat out. It is letting the heat out into the whole street.
The brick that holds it open is the only brick in the building not doing something more important.
Outside, a cart with BREAD painted on the side, slightly wrong. The bread's right. The painting isn't.
LISTEN_TO: The yard, and a cart being loaded. Bread leaving for everywhere at once.
A horse in the yard, shifting, waiting for its load.
Somebody out back, counting loaves aloud. He gets to forty and starts again.
